messages:
Maya: Quick sync  I noticed this week's KPI board shows a big spike in sessions after the launch posts but downstream MQLs barely budged. Can we triage before the weekly review?
Ethan: Seen it. My hunch is split attribution + landing-template differences. We ran three CTA variants and two short-form templates.
Priya: Also the webinar invite used a partner redirect for registrations which doesn't surface utm_campaign; that will push traffic into 'referral' by default.
Maya: Ugh. Can someone run a reconciled view (utm_source vs referrer vs landing_template) so we can see where the session lift actually maps?
Ethan: Running a quick pull now. If you want to reuse, here's the SQL I ran to map sessions->landing->utm:
```
SELECT date_trunc('day', occurred_at) AS day, coalesce(utm_source,'(none)') AS utm, referrer_domain, landing_template, count(DISTINCT user_id) AS sessions, sum(is_lead::int) AS leads, sum(is_mql::int) AS mqls
FROM page_events
WHERE occurred_at >= '2026-05-04' AND occurred_at < '2026-05-11'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
ORDER BY day, sessions DESC;
```
Priya: Nice. Preliminary output: home-hero drove most MQLs, social-compact had big sessions but low leads, partner_redirect domain accounted for ~14% of sessions and shows up as referral with utm_missing.
Maya: That aligns with a pattern we saw last quarter. Two asks: 1) can AnalyticsBot add an annotation to the KPI board explaining the partner redirect and CTA variants? 2) Ops, can we standardize the redirect passthrough to preserve utm params?
OpsBot: Noted. I'll open a tracking ticket for the partner redirect passthrough and add an annotation now.
AnalyticsBot: Annotation created on kpi-weekly: "2026-05-07 partner redirect traffic stripped utm params; multiple CTA variants used across launch posts. May distort utm_campaign attribution and short-term MQL comparisons."
Ethan: Another nuance  the short-form landing template intentionally delays MQL assignment until a nurture event. Those registrations are good signal but won't show as MQL immediately. We should surface registration->mql lag in KPI notes.
Priya: I'll produce a small cohort table showing median time-to-MQL by landing_template and attach the CSV to the KPI thread. Expect it by Monday 08:30 PT.
Maya: Great. Also, can we avoid reusing utm_campaign names for A/B creatives? That made campaign tiles noisy. Could we add a tiny naming guideline to the marketing playbook?
OpsBot: Ticket created: MARK-742 - enforce utm naming template in campaign creation flow.
AnalyticsBot: Quick pull summary:
- sessions +27% WoW
- leads +5% WoW
- MQLs +1% WoW
- partner_redirect domain = 13.7% sessions, 2% MQLs
- short-form landing median time-to-MQL = 9 days, hero-full median = 3 days
Ethan: Action items: Priya reconcile utm/referrer CSV, Ops to fix passthrough and MARK-742, Maya to draft a one-paragraph benchmark note for Monday explaining attribution noise + form-timing differences.
Maya: Will draft the benchmark narrative and add it to the KPI commentary. Draft line: "Apparent session lift primarily from referral/partner traffic and compact social templates; downstream MQLs reflect landing-template timing and partner tracking gaps rather than a material drop in funnel health."
Priya: CSV posted: https://files.redwood.com/marketing/reconciled_attrib_1799009999.csv
OpsBot: MARK-742 created and assigned to frontend-team for partner redirect passthrough. ETA: two sprints.
Maya: Thanks all. We'll present the reconciled numbers and the narrative in the weekly KPI review. Closing this thread unless anyone spots an urgent blocker. :thumbsup:
